securityInvariants.statement: At protocol versions 1, 2, 3 and 5, finalized non-genesis blocks require unique configured-validator attestations at floor(2N/3)+1 quorum.
A non-zero consensus round requires sequential predecessor skip-quorum evidence; rounds cannot be jumped without certified evidence.

At protocol-v6 heights a block is final only with floor(2N/3)+1 distinct configured-validator commit votes for one (chainId, height, commitRound, blockHash) under the commit-vote signing domain; v6 blocks carry an empty roundCertificate and legacy attestations are rejected.

A protocol-v6 round change requires a timeout certificate of quorum timeout votes for the previous round that carries the maximum reported prepare QC; a validator prepare-votes only its locked block or a proposal justified by a strictly higher-round prepare QC (SAFE-VOTE), and the next leader must re-propose the block of that QC.
Validator signing reserves durable anti-equivocation state before local or remote signing output is requested.

Signing-journal compaction removes only reservations at or below the durably finalized height and atomically persists retained reservations before reducing in-memory anti-equivocation state; persistence ambiguity fail-stops validator signing.

Protocol-v6 validators durably reserve at most one value per (height, round, step) in signing-journal v2 rows before signing, persist the lock and commit rows in one fsynced append after the prepare QC file, never lower a lock, and may always sign one timeout per round after an earlier prepare or commit; legacy binaries fail closed on v2 rows.
Chain ID, genesis identity, protocol version and active validator schedule are validated before accepting consensus history.
Block validation re-executes transactions and requires the deterministic authenticated state root committed by the block.

Total issuance is fixed at genesis and can never exceed 50M ZYN: no post-genesis issuance path exists (mining is retired under every protocol version), and transaction-fee burns permanently reduce supply without creating issuance headroom.

An activity settlement pays at most 10,000 ZYN, settles only the most recently closed 24-hour epoch by block time, and epochs settle once and in strictly increasing order, so one oracle key moves at most 10,000 ZYN per epoch.

When genesis declares activityOracleThreshold m, an activity settlement is valid on every path only with signatures from at least m distinct registered oracle keys over the canonical payload {chainId, sender, epoch, entries, receiptRoot}; without it, settlements carrying oracleApprovals are rejected and single-oracle behaviour is unchanged.

When genesis declares allocationLocks, no block or mempool path lets the founder account fall below its still-locked allocation (365-day cliff, then 1,095-day linear release measured by block timestamp from genesis), and the permanent-liquidity account can never be debited.

Mining is retired: every mining_claim transaction is rejected under protocol versions 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 by transaction validation, mempool admission, block production, block and proposal validation and both the legacy and State-v2 appliers; the former protocol-v5 proof-of-work binding is historical audit context only.
No mining claim can be admitted to the mempool or finalized in any block, the scheduled mining reward is always zero, and the reserved mining tracker remains zero-balance and non-spendable.
Checkpoint/state installation requires independently supplied finalized-tip and snapshot-digest anchors and validates the restored chain through the normal recovery path.
Native P2P authenticates node identity and binds peers to chain/genesis while enforcing bounded streams, frames, work and sync responses.
Non-loopback RPC is fail-closed unless consensus authentication and an exact HTTPS-enforcing trusted proxy are configured.
Validator-set and protocol updates require current-set quorum authorization and delayed activation; unsupported activated protocol versions fail closed.
After quorum-authorized validator-key replacement activates, the retired key is no longer an active consensus signer and the replacement set persists across restart.
